note.seg: Hs. Co p. 31, der um 1330 Or (Oxford Oriel Coll. 46 f. 99) folgt. Aus Co excerpirt Lambard Αρχαιονομια (1568, Praef. Ciiii; ed. Wheloc p. 220; ed. Wilkins Leg. Anglo-Sax. p. 422, daraus Houard Anc. loix Franç. II 456), den Lindenbrog{*} Codex leg. antiq., Exorcism. 3 ohne Citat wiederholt. Diesem folgen Baluze (daraus Walter Corp. iur. Germ. III 574 und Rozière Form. n. 601) und Zeumer 719. Ferner excerpirt Co: [Parker] Antiq. Brit. eccl. (1572), ed. 1605 p. 103, und aus ähnl. Hs. übersetzt XVI W. Harrison Descr. of Britaine (vor Holinshed Chron. of Engl., 1577) II 9. ¶ Dieser Ordo ist in England nach 1066 (s. u. S. 429ᵃ·ᵇ·ᶜ) compilirt oder überarbeitet.

MS Co p. 31, which is followed by Or (Oxford Oriel Coll. 46 f. 99) of c. 1330. Lambard, Αρχαιονομια (1568, Praef. Ciiii; ed. Wheloc p. 220; ed. Wilkins Leg. Anglo-Sax. p. 422, whence Houard Anc. loix Franç. II 456), excerpts from Co; Lindenbrog{*} Codex leg. antiq., Exorcism. 3 repeats him without citation. He is followed by Baluze (whence Walter Corp. iur. Germ. III 574 and Rozière Form. n. 601) and Zeumer 719. Co is also excerpted by [Parker] Antiq. Brit. eccl. (1572), ed. 1605 p. 103, and XVI is translated from a similar MS by W. Harrison Descr. of Britaine (prefixed to Holinshed Chron. of Engl., 1577) II 9. ¶ This ordo was compiled or revised in England after 1066 (see below p. 429ᵃ·ᵇ·ᶜ).

Memorandum, quod iudicium ferri candentis est ad purgacionem hominum liberorum, et iudicium aque est ad homines rusticos; et hoc inuenies in Legibus H[enrici] regis secundi in penultimo folio am oberen Rande Co, im Text Or. Hiermit wird citirt Ran. Glanvilla XIV 1, 8: per ferrum calidum, si homo liber, per aquam, si fuerit rusticus, in Co p. 167. Vgl. oben XVᵇ. [Dennoch ward 1177 quidam nobilissimus et ditissimus ciuium Londoniarum Iohannes Senex per iudicium aque se mundare verurtheilt und dann gehängt, quia per iudicium aque perierat. (Gesta Henr. II. ed. Stubbs I 156)]. Dieses Memorandum behandelt das Ordal als giltig (während Nachträge in Co Or es per Innocentium III, tempore regis Iohannis abgeschafft nennen), gehört also vielleicht dem Compilator der Leges Anglor. s. XIII. in. Lond. coll. (ed. Liebermann p. 23). Der neben Co Or dritte Codex dieser Leges hat die Ordalien nicht.

Memorandum, quod iudicium ferri candentis est ad purgacionem hominum liberorum, et iudicium aque est ad homines rusticos; et hoc inuenies in Legibus H[enrici] regis secundi in penultimo folio in the upper margin Co, in the text Or. This cites Ran. Glanvilla XIV 1, 8: per ferrum calidum, si homo liber, per aquam, si fuerit rusticus, in Co p. 167. Cf. above XVᵇ. [Nevertheless, in 1177 quidam nobilissimus et ditissimus ciuium Londoniarum Iohannes Senex was condemned per iudicium aque se mundare and was then hanged, quia per iudicium aque perierat. (Gesta Henr. II. ed. Stubbs I 156)]. This Memorandum treats the ordeal as valid (whereas additions in Co Or describe it as abolished per Innocentium III, tempore regis Iohannis), and so perhaps belongs to the compiler of the Leges Anglor. s. XIII. in. Lond. coll. (ed. Liebermann p. 23). The third codex of these Leges, besides Co Or, does not contain the ordeals.

Das Memorandum I 427{b} gehört den Leges Anglorum (ebd. Z. 4 v. u.) nicht; denn deren älteste Hs. Rylands zu Manchester hat das Ordal ebensowenig wie K 2; vgl. EHR 1913 p. 737 l. 5. Man streiche also I 427 Z. 4 v. u. die Zeile ‘gehört—23’

The Memorandum I 427{b} does not belong to the Leges Anglorum (ibid. l. 4 from bottom); for their oldest MS, Rylands at Manchester, lacks the ordeal just as K 2 does; cf. EHR 1913 p. 737 l. 5. The line ‘gehört—23’ in I 427 l. 4 from bottom should therefore be deleted
